about.title: Madera Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Madera County sees a steady share of injury collisions each year, with public records showing roughly 180 injury crashes and 247 people hurt in the most recent reporting year. Corridors like Rt 145, Cleveland Avenue W, Tozer Street, and Cleveland Avenue tend to show up often in local crash counts, and reports cluster around Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., when commuter and weekend traffic overlap. If you were injured in one of these collisions, the days right after matter: insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, vehicle damage, and witness memories fade quickly. LawProactive is a free connection service — not a law firm — that puts injured Madera residents in touch with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency. There's no cost to you unless your case results in a recovery, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a public road authority — is involved. Waiting too long can permanently close the door on compensation.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery can be reduced by whatever percentage of blame is assigned to you. An early recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used to inflate your share of fault, which is why it's worth speaking with an attorney first.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases. An attorney can help make sure evidence supporting those harms is preserved before it disappears.

items.question: I was in a crash on Cleveland Avenue — should I give the other driver's insurance company a statement?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use early statements to shift blame or minimize your claim. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to share.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Madera car accident?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, such as a city or county road agency, contributed to the crash, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's wise to act quickly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule allows you to recover damages even if you were partly responsible, though your compensation may be reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.
